newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to sell 26 pct stake in bus maker - company.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to sell 26 pct stake in bus maker - company.

text.p: Ukraine's State Property Fund plans to offer for sale to a strategic investor 26 percent of shares in the country's only bus manufacturer, the company's chief executive said.

"The government understands that realistically Ukrainian bus companies cannot succeed on their own, so we must seek foreign investors," Stepan Davydyak of the Lvivsky Avtobusny Zavod (LAZ) told Reuters.

Davydyak said the State Property Fund, the state privatisation agency, approved the privatisation plan to retain 25 percent of shares in state hands, and to auction 26 percent of shares to Ukrainians through privatisation certificates.
Five percent of shares were allotted to company management and 18 percent of shares were purchased by the workers' collective and two other companies, he added.

The Lviv bus manufacturer, which held the monopoly for manufacture of petrol-powered city and inter-city buses in the former Soviet Union, is one of 208 government-designated companies to be privatised through strategic investment.
Under rules for tender, investors are required to upgrade the company and make it profitable within a designated period.
Starting capital in the enterprise has been valued at 4.8 million hryvnias, said Davydyak.
The company recently started building electrically-powered trolley buses, and plans to increase overall production to 5,000 buses by 2000, he added.
Davydyak said the foreign investors have not come forward yet, and blamed problems of old equipment at the factory and an unstable world market for buses.

The bus maker has been working sporadically this year and is expected to produce 1,200 buses by the end of 1996, down from 2,148 buses manufactured in 1995. Davydyak also said workers have not been paid in the last two months.
